note: Axes that HOLD per the repo's own benchmark. The Dial lists an entry only when its axis file is on disk. tier=essential entries are listed first under Essentials, ordered by visible_impact (top-dose saturation shift + peak luminance shift + |edge ratio - 1|, all from study/data/axes.csv); tier=subtle entries come next under Subtle: they hold, but show little visible change in our renders. fallback_safe_max is used when the axis file's header does not record safe_max (it is the highest strength tested and held).

axes.label: Corridor orientation
axes.evidence: study/data/axes.csv: strict_push=holds, monotone=yes, edge ratio at top dose 1.980, saturation 0.486; highest strength tested (and held) = 9.5532. Pre-registered criterion: docs/EXPERIMENTS.md section F.

axes.evidence: docs/EXPERIMENTS.md section E (fair benchmark, seeds 11 and 23): at 0.5 the frame brightens (lum +0.16) and loses detail (edge -21%) with framing intact; safe_max 0.25 is where framing holds, wash is visible at 0.5.
